label: prop:q-beta-c-k-recursion-from-habiro-q-difference
title: $c_k$ precision-ladder recursion induced by the fibre-level Habiro $q$-difference equation — depth-$d$ linear recursion on $c_k$ from the $q$-shift kernel $R(q,\xi)$ acting on $F(\xi)$
html:
Let F(q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]^\wedge be a fibre-level Habiro element associated to the operator-valued T_\beta selection (Min-Frobenius-norm collapse: T_β = S · 1 under the canonical Markov-trace inner product on H_n(R, q)). Let F(q) satisfy a q-difference equation of depth d:

F(q\xi) \;=\; R(q,\xi)\cdot F(\xi), \qquad R(q,\xi) \in \mathbb{Q}(q)[\xi, \xi^{-1}] \text{ of degree} \le d.

The precision-ladder coefficients c_k satisfy a depth-d linear recursion:

c_{k+1} \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{d} a_j(q_0)\cdot c_{k+1-j}, \qquad a_j(q_0) \in \mathbb{Q}(q_0),

with kernel coefficients \{a_j\} extracted from R(q_0, \xi) via the (u;u)_m \to u^k Habiro change-of-basis.

The existence of such a recursion is a hypothesis on F. For the colored Jones function of a knot, a nonzero linear q-difference recursion, with coefficients polynomial in q^{\pm 1} and q^n, always exists (it is q-holonomic, [garoufalidis-le-2005, Thm. 1]); that F is of this kind is not established here, and that theorem gives no bound on the depth d.

The operator content is T_\beta = S \cdot \mathbf{1}, with S pinned by the SDP constraint. The selector direction is S-independent and q-rational. The scalar S = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta/E_0 is not the ladder normalization. Together, these define F(q) = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta(q)/[Q_A(q) \cdot \cos(\alpha_{\mathrm{eff}}(q))] as a single fibre-level Habiro object. Its q-difference structure generates the c_k.

The sequence c_2, \ldots, c_8 collapses to the structural seed c_2 = -1 and a kernel R(q_0, \xi) of bounded degree d. The recursion generates c_3, \ldots, c_8 automatically.

Write the recursion coefficients as elementary symmetric polynomials a_j = e_j(\{r_\lambda\}) of the per-mode rates r_\lambda = (q-1)\mu_\lambda. Under the bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1} the prefactor is not bar-odd: q-1 \mapsto q^{-1}-1 = -(q-1)/q. It is bar-odd only up to the monomial twist q, (q^{-1}-1)\,q = -(q-1) (the j=1 case of the Habiro-basis monomial twist). If every \mu_\lambda is bar-even, a product of j rates therefore picks up the sign (-1)^j and the twist q^j. Then a_j is bar-even for even j and bar-odd for odd j, up to q^j. Both qualifications are part of the claim. The twist is not optional, and bar-evenness of the \mu_\lambda is a hypothesis that is not established here. Under them, the alternation is the structural law behind the ladder's parity bookkeeping.

The cyclotomic factors \Phi_d for d \in \{2,3,6\} and for all primes p are self-reciprocal. Divisibility by \Phi_n is invariant under the bar involution for every n > 1. The identity \Phi_n(1/q)\,q^{\varphi(n)} = \Phi_n(q) guarantees period-3 closure.

The Habiro element F(q) is the trace of the q-heat kernel over the Hecke modules:

Z_q(t) = \sum_{\lambda \in \Lambda} d_\lambda(q) \cdot \exp_q(-\mu_\lambda(q) \cdot t).

The q-difference equation for F(q) derives from the depth-1 Jackson equations of each mode. The net partition function satisfies a q-difference equation of depth |\Lambda|. The c_k coefficients are extracted at q_0.

At the fibre level, Z_q is a Hahn--Exton q-Bessel function. The coefficients c_k obey the q-Bessel second-order q-difference equation. This identification applies at the fibre level only. Archimedean closure of c_3 via a substrate-fixed q-Bessel is refuted. The q-Bessel object lives in the brane-tower limit.
